source.title: What’s up with LLMs representing XORs of arbitrary features?

record.file_problem: The post is present in full. Some referenced figures and their numerical values are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on linear-probe access to XORs of features, but does not measure whether individual neurons have multiple unrelated response meanings, or test any of the listed versions. Its experiments concern a related representation question.
record.gate_note: The post reports probe results for XOR features, including a comparison with a reset network. These results are recorded as findings about a related construct under fits_no_version. Comments reporting other people's experiments, and the post author's later comment referring to results whose values are not given in the text, are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The post probes residual-stream representations of LLaMA-2-13B for XORs of binary features. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, how often they do, or what causes it. Superposition is mentioned only in a footnote. No version of the polysemantic-neuron claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. The author concludes that LLMs seem to compute and linearly represent XORs of arbitrary features even without an obvious reason, calls this surprising, and says it is probably a bad sign for probe-based interpretability. The reset-network result leads him to reject a purely incidental, random-features explanation. He remains confused about the mechanism and leans towards an explanation that aggregates noisy signals from correlated features.
record.recipe_differences: The original sources concern neuron feature visualization and softmax linear units; this post uses linear probes to classify XORs of binary features in residual-stream representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports variations in dataset construction and feature placement, and contrasts the trained LLaMA-2-13B with a reset version. It does not provide per-condition numerical comparisons for all variations.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on LLaMA-2-13B layer-14 residual-stream representations classify XORs of arbitrary binary features, such as has_alice XOR has_not, with near-perfect accuracy. On a weight-shuffled (reset) network, the XOR probe does not beat the 0.75 accuracy obtainable from an OR probe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained LLMs make XORs of arbitrary linearly represented features linearly decodable from the residual stream, and this depends on training rather than on random high-dimensional structure.

record.problems: Numerical accuracies for the main experiments are not stated in the supplied text, and several results are referred to through visualizations that are not included. The reported reset-network comparison uses an OR-probe baseline; the post does not report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No explicit result values are given for the author's later comment describing a 10,000-input experiment, so it was not included as a row. Results in commenters' reports are not results from this study.

untested.parts: All: no vision models or single-neuron analyses.
All: no measurement of MLP neuron responses or of their prevalence by layer.
All: superposition is mentioned only in a footnote, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6 / discusses classification is correct. The author's later comment reports a rerun on 10,000 inputs with no numbers in the text, and Clément Dumas's comment reports a Pythia-70m result; neither is a study result here. The rows' 'observed' states describe the post's XOR claim, not any version, so they are set to cannot_determine with respect to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The prevalence of polysemantic MLP neurons in language models; the post probes feature labels rather than measuring neuron responses to tokens or contexts.
Whether capacity pressure or superposition causes neuron polysemanticity. The post discusses possible explanations but does not test this causal account.
Whether initialization, regularization, or training noise causes polysemantic neurons when capacity is sufficient.
Effects of activation function, architecture, or regularization on the share of polysemantic neurons and performance.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect shared features or related jobs when examined with better tools.
How activation range or explanation-scoring choices affect whether a neuron is counted as polysemantic.
